newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha inches up in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha inches up in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Naphtha prices edged up in late afternoon Tokyo trade on Thursday mirroring overnight crude gains, but trading remained lacklustre as market players began to leave for Christmas holidays, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half February was notionally assessed at $238.00/240.00, compared to late Wednesday's $237.50/239.00.
First-half March was quoted at $235.00/237.00. It was sold to a Japanese trading house at $235.00 on Wednesday.
The one-month spread from first-half February was discussed at plus $6.50/7.00, compared with Wednesday's plus $6.00/7.00.
In physical naphtha, trading for second-half January cargoes got into full swing, with premiums assessed at around $7.00, traders with petrochemical manufacturers said.

In the low-sulphur waxy residue market, traders expected Pertamina to announce its initial allocation for January lifting cargoes earlier than usual due to Christmas holidays. They said the allotment may be announced as early as Friday.

Japan's ethylene demand in the first half of 1997 is expected to rise by 2.5 percent from a year ago to 3.55 million tonnes in line with gradual growth in the economy, the Trade Ministry said. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
